title: Tenant usage fairness corrector and late-arrival credit applier
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We occasionally receive usage events that arrive after the window used by the primary real-time ingestor (streaming gateway) has been compacted into interim ledgers. These late events cause unfair per-tenant cost allocations (e.g., small tenants either get overcharged when a later large session is attributed to them or under-credited when credits arrive after a billing window). The goal of this ticket is to build a correctness job — the Tenant Usage Fairness Corrector (TUFC) — that incrementally applies late-arrival adjustments and tenant credits without reprocessing full windows, keeps charges idempotent, and produces explainable audit records for billing and customer support.
problem_statement: Late-arrival events and out-of-order streaming batches lead to per-tenant allocation drift between the streaming ledger and the finalized billing rollup. Manual fixes are slow and opaque. We need an automated, time-bounded, auditable correction pass that: 1) computes delta adjustments for affected invoices/snapshots, 2) applies tenant credits or debits, 3) emits reconcile events for downstream billing systems and the Console ledger UI, and 4) preserves guarantees for no-double-charge and deterministic convergence.
technical_approach: Design: TUFC will run as an incremental map-reduce style job that operates on compacted interim partitions. Steps: (1) Identify affected partitions by consulting the 'late-event index' emitted by the streaming gateway watermarking logic. (2) For each partition, compute an idempotent delta by joining compacted records with raw late events keyed by session_id and model_variant. (3) Normalize token costs by model variant + quantization profile to compute monetary deltas. (4) Emit three outputs: (a) billing_delta_stream (for downstream charge adjustment), (b) audit_patch_records (append-only records for Console/Support), (c) metrics and refund candidates for Customer Success. Implementation notes: use event time watermarks with a 72h max-late bound, leverage existing compaction job's checkpoint metadata, and store idempotency keys as 'correction_epoch:<partition_id>:<run_id>'. The job will be written in Scala as a Spark streaming batch job for efficiency and re-used in airflow orchestration with a dedicated SLO/alerting pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: 1) TUFC can process a 48h backlog partition (typical worst-case) in under 30 minutes in staging with a synthetic dataset.
2) End-to-end test that inserts synthetic late events causes exactly the expected monetary delta for a tenant and produces an audit_patch_record with the original and corrected token counts.
3) Correction runs are idempotent: re-running the same correction epoch produces no additional billing_delta_stream messages.
4) Console shows a human-readable audit row for each applied correction and links to the originating events and PRs.
5) Monitoring: SLOs for job latency (P50 < 12m, P95 < 30m) and success rate (> 99%).
tasks: Define schema for audit_patch_records and billing_delta_stream and add to schema-registry
Prototype diff logic in a local Spark notebook against compacted partition sample
Implement TUFC job with incremental checkpointing and idempotency key writes
Add integration test that injects late events into streaming gateway and validates downstream deltas
Create Console UI hooks to display audit records and provide a "revert" metadata link
Add alerts and dashboards: job latency, processed-partitions, idempotency-failures, applied-dollars
Coordinate with Billing team to accept billing_delta_stream messages and map to invoice adjustments
comments: 2025-01-12 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: Billing + Streaming + Console teams present. Agreed on 72h watermark as conservative default and to surface a config toggle per-customer for enterprise customers.
2025-01-18 - Marcus Nguyen: Spike completed — local notebook shows joins are dominated by a small hot set of session_ids; caching session metadata reduces runtime by ~3x.
2025-01-24 - Joanna Li (Billing): Review: requested explicit refund candidate flag for >$5 adjustments and a manual approval workflow. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-01-29 - Marcus Nguyen: Implemented prototype that writes billing_delta_stream to Kafka topic 'billing.corrections.v1' and registered schema under 'billing.corrections.v1' in schema-registry. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/428

2025-02-02 - Design review: Console audit row schema reviewed. UX asks for original token breakdown, corrected token breakdown, reason code, and linked event IDs. Design: DES-210 will provide the visual layout.

2025-02-05 - Marcus Nguyen: Integration test flakiness discovered with concurrent compaction — added a preflight check to ensure compaction checkpoint is immutable for the partition before applying corrections.
rollout_plan: 1) Run TUFC nightly in staging against 7-day synthetic backlog; 2) Run in a shadow mode in production where billing_delta_stream is written to an alternative topic 'billing.corrections.shadow' for two weeks; 3) Run a small customer pilot (1% of tenants) with actual invoice adjustments disabled but audit records visible to Support; 4) Gradually enable adjustments for low-risk tenants, then enterprise customers after manual approval flow is in place.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Applying a bad delta could overcharge customers. Mitigation: Start in shadow mode, add 'max-delta-threshold' that flags adjustments > $50 for manual review, and maintain full-rollback metadata. Risk: Long-running joins causing SLA violations. Mitigation: Pre-aggregate by session_id and use materialized caches for top-k sessions.
support_instructions: Support can read audit_patch_records from the Console -> Billing Corrections tab. For a disputed charge, open INC-<tenant_id>-TUFC and attach audit_patch_record JSON. Run the TUFC 'replay' with a specific run_id to reproduce the adjustment in staging.
next_steps: Finish schema registration, complete TUFC implementation PR, create integration test harness linked to streaming gateway dev cluster, and schedule pilot run for 2025-02-20.
